sections.html:
Cedar County is rural southwest Missouri. Stockton is the seat, El Dorado Springs is the largest town, and none of the population counts as urban, so a house here is usually in a small town or on open land. Stockton Lake takes up a good share of the county's water area. Two school districts serve it, El Dorado Springs R-II and Stockton R-I.

  • Population, July 1, 2025: 14,888, with 6,985 housing units and 74.1% owner-occupied.
  • Middle value of owner-occupied homes (2020 to 2024): $168,100.
  • Median gross rent: $767. Median household income: $48,181.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 8.

Only 8 permits in a year means very little new construction competes with resale houses, so condition and price carry most of the weight with buyers.

Two elected offices split the work. The Assessor values property. The Collector of Revenue mails bills and collects the money. Neither sets the rate. That comes from the school, fire, ambulance and other districts listed on each statement.

  • Collector of Revenue: 113 South Street, PO Box 280, Stockton, MO 65785, in Room 1 on the main floor of the courthouse. Phone 417.276.6700 ext. 224, fax 417.276.4658.
  • Assessor: courthouse line 417-276-6700. Extensions 258 and 259 take personal property questions.
  • Online payments and bill search run through the Collector's page on cedarcountymo.gov.

The Assessor's own site, cedar.missouriassessors.com, has the parcel search, the real estate and personal property FAQs and the newsletters.

sections.h2: Due dates and how to pay
sections.html:
Statements for land, buildings and personal property are mailed in November. Payment is due by December 31, and for mailed checks the postmark decides. A postmark after December 31 has to include penalty and interest, and the delinquent payment chart on your statement shows the add-on. If December 1 comes and no bill has shown up, call the Collector, since a missing bill doesn't erase the obligation.

  • Online payments carry a 2.4 percent card convenience fee, or a $1.95 fee for an e-check.
  • A mailed payment's receipt takes 7 to 10 days. Online receipts can be printed once the payment posts.
  • A prepay plan divides last year's amount into nine equal installments. You must start by September 30, and the November statement then shows what is left.
  • Personal property is valued on January 1, and the whole year's tax is owed even after the owner moves away.

Real estate tax stays attached to the parcel itself, whoever the owner is.

sections.h2: How the Assessor sets home values
sections.html:
Real property is reassessed every odd-numbered year, and in even years the office adds new construction. Values reflect the property's condition on January 1, so a building torn down after that date is still taxed for the full year. Because 2027 is an odd year, plan for a reassessment then.

Field staff look at the outside of buildings and go inside only if the owner asks. RSMo 137.130 gives the Assessor a right to inspect when information is missing. In 2025 the State Tax Commission ordered a 14.99 percent increase on improved residential and commercial property in the county, with new construction excepted, and Change in Value notices went out in June 2025. If your house sold or was refinanced since, expect a number well above older figures.

Personal property sheets are due before March 1, with late penalties from $15 up to $105 depending on assessed value. The Assessor offers e-filing with the account number and ePIN printed on the sheet.

Begin by phoning the Assessor to walk through the value. If you still disagree, the next stops are the county board that hears valuation appeals and then the State Tax Commission. Ask the Cedar County Clerk or the Assessor for the board's current forms and hearing dates.

StepTiming
Informal review with the AssessorAfter the Change in Value notice arrives
Hearing request to the county board (RSMo 137.275)Lodged by the second Monday of July
Appeal to the State Tax Commission (RSMo 138.430)Within the statutory window or a month after the board decides, whichever comes later

One rule helps an owner whose value jumped. RSMo 138.060 says the board starts with no presumption that the Assessor's number is right. When assessed valuation rose at least 15 percent from the last assessment, the burden of proof falls on the Assessor, unless the rise came from new construction or improvements.

sections.h2: Tax relief for seniors and others
sections.html:
Cedar County adopted the Senate Bill 190 senior tax freeze. Senior tax credit applications are taken from March 15 to May 15, 2027. Seniors and people who are 100 percent disabled can also ask the Assessor for a 948 form, a credit based on the real estate taxes paid during the year.

Disabled-veteran exemptions are a separate matter. Rules have been changing at the state level, and the Assessor says it will apply any new exemption as soon as the law allows. Ask the Assessor before assuming an exemption covers your parcel.

The Collector holds a delinquent land tax sale on the fourth Monday of August each year and issues certificates of purchase and redemptions. Land with back taxes can end up in that sale, so clear the balance or tell the title company early.

  • Ask the Collector for the current balance on the parcel, including penalty and interest.
  • Give the title company the Collector's contact details so the payoff shows up on the settlement statement.
  • After the deed is recorded, tell the Collector and the Assessor the buyer's name and mailing address so the next bill reaches the right person.

Since tax liability stays with the land, a buyer inherits an unpaid balance unless it is settled at closing. Paying it from proceeds keeps your closing clean. Bring the parcel number from your latest statement to the title company, along with the Collector's phone number, so the payoff letter can be ordered the same day you sign the listing. A cash buyer can also take on a parcel with back taxes and let the closing agent settle them, which avoids a lender's demand that the account be cleared first.

faqs.q: When are Cedar County property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 31 each year. Statements are mailed in November, and the postmark on a mailed payment decides whether it is on time. After December 31, penalty and interest apply. If no bill has come by December 1, call 417.276.6700 ext. 224 in Stockton.

faqs.q: Which office answers questions about my value?
faqs.a: The Cedar County Assessor, at 417-276-6700. Personal property questions go to ext. 258 or 259. The Assessor's website has the real estate FAQ, the parcel search and the latest newsletter. The Collector is a separate office and cannot change a value on a statement.

Use the Pay/Search link on the Collector's page at cedarcountymo.gov. Cards carry a 2.4 percent convenience fee and e-checks a $1.95 fee. Search by last name then first name with no comma, and print the receipt once the payment is applied.

faqs.q: Can I challenge my property value?
faqs.a: Yes. Talk to the Assessor first, then lodge a hearing request with the county board no later than the second Monday of July, as RSMo 137.275 requires. A further appeal to the State Tax Commission is open within the statutory window or a month after the board decides, whichever comes later.

faqs.q: What if the land has delinquent taxes when I sell?
faqs.a: Pay the balance at or before closing, usually through the title company, because the lien follows the land. The Collector holds a delinquent land tax sale on the fourth Monday of August. Get the exact payoff, with penalty and interest, from the Collector in Stockton.
